items.summary: A new high-resolution modeling tool is offering one of the clearest pictures yet of how climate change could affect a vital part of the marine food chain in Northwest European seas. items.title: New fiber laser combines ultrashort pulses with broad spectrum and stable output
items.summary: Femtosecond lasers produce pulses lasting only quadrillionths of a second. Their speed makes them useful for imaging rapid processes, sampling high-frequency signals and measuring distance or time with high precision. items.title: Bacteria split their membranes to kill infected cells and block viral spread, study shows
items.summary: A new study reveals a previously unknown bacterial immune mechanism in which the signaling molecule 2′,3′-cGAMP triggers the splitting of the bacterial membrane into two distinct bilayers, leading to the death of infected cells and preventing further phage propagation.

items.title: Countries agree on new ways to achieve safe chemical use
items.summary: Countries have agreed on new measures to speed up efforts aimed at preventing the harmful effects of chemical products on health and the environment, the U.N. said.

items.title: Proteins with ancient viral roots guard genetic switches left by mobile DNA
items.summary: Much of our genome contains mobile pieces or "transposable elements": pieces of DNA that spread and accumulated over millions of years, some originating from ancient viruses. Although many are no longer mobile, their sequences can influence when nearby genes switch on or off.

items.title: Study reveals surge-detachment sequence at Dehdal Glacier in Pamir Mountains
items.summary: Researchers have reconstructed a surge–detachment sequence at Dehdal Glacier in the Pamir Mountains of Tajikistan, revealing how a period of rapid glacier acceleration culminated in two successive large-scale ice-detachment events.
